activity.lede: What each earner container does on the network: how many connections it opens, how many fail, which ports and networks it talks to, and whether it reaches into your own network or sends mail. It is off until you switch it on for a box. Every 5 minutes the box starts one short-lived helper per earner that reads the kernel's socket tables and connection counters. It never reads what is inside the traffic, the names looked up, or the sites visited.

activity.sampling_html: Connection counts are complete; destinations are sampled (5 snapshots over 8 s every 5 min), so short connections are counted but may be missing from the list. UDP without a fixed peer shows no destination. Remote addresses are kept for 24 hours, the totals by port, network and country for 35 days. Everything stays on this server; network names come from a table downloaded to it. How it works

fleet.fence.confirm:
Turn on LAN isolation on "{name}"?

- The worker creates a Docker network (cashpilot-isolated) and one firewall table (ip cashpilot) on its host.
- Each running earner on Docker's default bridge is redeployed once onto that network. Storj gets its full clean stop first, so it can take a few minutes.
- Stopped earners stay stopped and move the next time you deploy them.
- Identities and data are kept: the same volumes and settings are used.

To undo it, set CASHPILOT_ISOLATION=off on the worker and redeploy the earners.
fleet.fence.failed: The LAN fence is not in place on this worker: {error}. While it is missing, earners on its network can reach this host's own services, and they may still reach the internet if another masquerade rule on the host covers them. Deploys are refused until it is back. To run without the fence, set CASHPILOT_ISOLATION=off on the worker.
fleet.fence.held: Held stopped: {list}. A missing LAN fence clears by itself; any other reason needs a redeploy from the dashboard.
fleet.fence.legacy: Earners on this worker can reach your LAN and this host: {names}.

fleet.fence.off: Isolation is off (CASHPILOT_ISOLATION=off). Earners still on the isolated network keep their internet; redeploy them to move them back to Docker's default bridge.
fleet.fence.on_failed: Isolation could not be turned on: {error}
fleet.fence.on_partial: {done} Could not move: {failed}. Redeploy or remove each from its service page.
fleet.fence.outside: These earners are still outside the isolated network and can reach your LAN: {names}.

To deploy to it from here, on its dashboard turn on "can start and stop services on this computer" and, on Windows, allow it through Windows Firewall. It also needs a private network or Tailscale address.

fleet.flag.duplicate_tip: More than one worker is registered under this name. That usually means this host was redeployed with a new or empty /data, so it re-registered under a new id and the old row stayed behind. Compare the ids and the last-seen times before removing one.
fleet.flag.enroll_incomplete_tip: This worker enrolled but never used its own key, so it is still authenticating with the shared CASHPILOT_API_KEY. The shared key is no longer accepted for it. It usually means the worker cannot persist /data/.worker_key: an old image, or a /data that is read-only or not a persistent volume. Upgrade it to 1.0.0+ with a writable persistent /data, then remove it here so it can enroll again.
fleet.flag.enrolling_tip: This worker has been issued its own key but has not used it yet, so the shared key still works for it for a short while. It clears itself on the worker's next heartbeat.

fleet.unfenced.confirm:
Redeploy {service} to move it behind the LAN fence?

- The worker reads the node's identity, replaces the container on the fenced network and checks the new one has the same identity.
- The data volume is kept. If the identity differs, the node is held stopped and the volume is left as it is.
- The node is down for under a minute.

fleet.unfenced.podman: It keeps running as it is. Podman cannot be fenced: run it on Docker with isolation on, or on your own network (CASHPILOT_CONTAINER_NETWORK).
fleet.unfenced.redeploy: Redeploy {service} to move behind the fence

settings.about.desc_html: CashPilot checks GitHub for the latest release. Update runs the documented docker compose pull && docker compose up -d for you, from a one-shot helper container — it installs the newest patch of the image series your compose file pins. Moving to a newer series still means editing the image tags: read UPGRADING.md first, then update the UI host first and every worker after it. Installs not managed by Compose get the manual commands instead.
settings.about.title: About and updates
settings.collection.desc: Credentials for automated earnings tracking. Only services with a built-in collector are shown. You don't need to deploy containers through CashPilot — just add your credentials.
settings.collection.title: Earnings collection
settings.earner_secrets.desc_html: Docker keeps a container's environment and command line in its settings, so docker inspect, a backup of Docker's folder and any tool with the Docker socket show every earner password in plain text. With CASHPILOT_EARNER_SECRETS=file on a worker, the earners it deploys get their passwords from a file that only the earner reads. Root on that machine can still read them, so this is not a wall against root. The guide lists which earners it covers.
settings.earner_secrets.how: Set it on the worker, recreate the worker container, then redeploy each earner from the dashboard. Remove the line to undo it: the next redeploy puts the values back in the environment.
settings.earner_secrets.title: Earner credentials on each box
settings.env.desc_html: These are read from the environment when CashPilot starts. Variables set via Docker -e flags are shown locked; the rest can be stored here, but a stored value does not take effect — set it in your compose file or Unraid template and restart. Several of them cannot change at runtime at all: the session key signs logins already in use, the data directory is where the open database lives, and the fleet key is what enrolled workers already hold.
settings.env.title: Environment
settings.heading: Settings
settings.health.desc: How old each stored credential is, and when it is expected to stop working. Credential values are never shown here — only which one it is and how it is doing.
settings.health.title: Credential health
settings.identities.desc: The device names and ids CashPilot deployed each service with, per box. They stay here after you remove a service, so you can find the device at the provider or give a new box the same id. Each value is hidden until you show or copy it, and every show is written to the audit log. Passwords, keys and wallet seeds are never kept here. You can change the id a box runs, add an id CashPilot did not deploy with, and download the whole list after you enter your password.
settings.identities.title: Device ids
settings.key.desc: One key decrypts every credential CashPilot stores. On a default install it sits in the data folder, next to the database it decrypts, so anyone with a copy of that folder can read your credentials. Keep the key outside the folder and a copy of the folder alone is no longer enough.
settings.key.step_check: Come back to this page. It checks that the key now comes from outside the data folder, and then offers to delete the copy that is still there.
settings.key.step_compose: Then add the secret to your compose file:
settings.key.step_file: Save the key in a file outside the data folder. The UI runs as user 1000, so that user must be able to read the file. With Docker Compose, put it in ./secrets/cashpilot_encryption_key next to your compose file:
settings.key.step_file_other_html: A secret manager works the same way: anything that writes the key to a file, or sets CASHPILOT_ENCRYPTION_KEY, will do. The guide has tested steps for Infisical, Vault, 1Password and Bitwarden.
settings.key.step_restart: Recreate the UI container, so it reads the new setting:
settings.key.step_reveal: Show the key and copy it. CashPilot asks for your password first and writes the reveal to the audit log.
settings.key.title: Credential encryption key
settings.restore.desc_html: Put a node identity or wallet back from a .cpbackup file made with a passphrase: Mysterium, ProxyBase or Anyone. The restore only creates a new container on a box that does not run the service, and never writes over a running one. To replace a running identity, download its backup first, then remove the service from that box on the dashboard and say yes when it asks to delete its data. Then restore here. Files sealed to a key, Storj and Sia use the command line steps.
